about: Sign-offs for the release gate (edakit gate). Each one counts only for the hash of its scope: 'circuit' = state_sha256 (graph, parts database, simulation config), 'layout' = layout_sha256 (layout files, artwork, footprint geometry), 'fab' = fab_sha256 (what the manufacturer builds from a gate run: Gerber layers, drill hits, BOM and CPL rows). When something there changes, it no longer counts – copy the new hash from the protocol header after the check was repeated. phase: 'export' blocks the release, 'order' and 'acceptance' come after the export. An accepted warning with scope 'decision' counts regardless of the hash and refers to a numbered decision in the docs. Parts are signed in their parts entry (field 'verified').

manual.text: Critical parts (U1 Nano pinout, C1 polarity, the 0805 LEDs' polarity, J1 servo pinout) checked a second time independently against datasheet and footprint – e.g. by the agent electrical-reviewer
manual.note: Confirmed for state 1ed944d2… on 2026-10-26: commit 0e95428 (D-16) adds only the purpose; check, sim and hints unchanged. OK for state ae05035e… (gate run 20261026-114752): KT-0805 LED polarity at LED0805-R-RD from five sources (datasheets p. 2, footprint triangle/chamfer, symbols, graph/pcb.json, polarity sheet), LED currents 5.8–9.0 mA red/yellow and 3.7–6.6 mA green against 25/30 mA, C1 C3359 16 V and pad 1 = plus (datasheet Fig. 1), J1 pad 1 GND / 2 +5V / 3 SERVO, rest byte-identical to the main board. Notes: the SMD header J1 holds less sideways pull – plug straight, tie the servo cable to the frame (D-11 stands); the greens are about 5x brighter than red/yellow (no change); wording in C41417360/C9900187880 for the next circuit change.

manual.text: Layout reviewed independently (manufacturability; mechanics: USB at the edge; operation of the buttons; looks of the LED row) on the manufacturing files of a gate run – e.g. by the agent pcb-reviewer
manual.note: Bound to fab hash 4e79e5c0… on 2026-10-28: the manufacturing files of the reviewed gate run 20261026-123018. Before, M-5 had scope 'layout', and since edakit f6dd9f7 the layout hash counts the artwork SVGs too (unchanged since 7667817), so it changed without a change of the board (D-20). OK for layout hash 67c811e0… (gate run 20261026-123018; first review of a0a80809… OK with notes, then keep-outs under the chevrons and the order-number placeholder under the Nano): smallest gap 0.206 mm (rule 0.203), copper 0.50 mm from the edge and 1.60 mm from the M3 cut-outs, tracks ≥ 0.557 mm from the Nano's NPTH holes, mask webs ≥ 0.136 mm, thermal spokes on every GND pad, polarity marks of LEDs/C1/J1 against P-2, silk ≥ 0.15 mm from openings. Notes: a tented GND via at (37.82, 48.00) sits on LED4's silk outline (cosmetic; a keep-out [37.2, 46.6, 38.4, 49.4] would move it); SMD J1 holds less sideways pull (D-11); order with 'Order Number (Specify Position)'.

manual.text: Regulatory review: circuit and parts against EU law for the stated purpose (RoHS, REACH, radio, batteries, product safety) – the agent regulatory-reviewer in its own session; support, not legal advice: no claim to correctness, nothing legally guaranteed
manual.note: OK for state 1ed944d2… and purpose private (D-16): no transmitter, 5 V USB only, no battery, no mains; RoHS and REACH data are not needed for own use. Notes: the firmware never detaches the servo, so a jam at rest stays an overload until unplugged (D-3) – detach it after the rest move; EMVG § 6 applies to own use too (disturb nothing, no formalities) – nothing to do for this board; at its end the bell goes to e-waste collection (ElektroG § 10).

manual.text: At JLCPCB after the upload: assembly preview (LEDs, C1, J1, buttons, resistors), BOM without missing parts, price
Acceptance of every delivered board: visual check, Nano plugged in, current through USB, every LED, both buttons, the servo swings
